clue.text: Deputy shortly has to compete with bereavement

blocks.note: deputy cut short to its first three letters
to rival someone is to compete with them

explanation.surface: A short-staffed deputy struggles to cope with a death in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' here means abbreviated, not soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Deprival is the state of having something taken away, as when a loved one dies.

clue.text: Record one's lines as part of serial

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
one is I, and the 's adds S
an ode is a poem, a set of lines

explanation.surface: An actor records their lines for a radio serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like an actor's script but stands for a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Each instalment of a serialised drama on television or radio is called an episode.

clue.text: This sort of questioning produces- - es speedy discharge

blocks.note: first meaning: questions fired off one after another without pause
second meaning: guns shooting in quick succession

explanation.surface: Relentless interrogation gets a suspect released quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes and 'es' after produces are smudges from the scanned newspaper; the clue reads 'produces speedy discharge'. 'Discharge' suggests release from custody; here it is gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both a barrage of quick questions and weapons shooting many rounds in quick succession.

clue.text: Patience, for example, is said to repay itself

blocks.note: surface: someone called Patience, or a card game, who pays herself back
setter's reading: the proverb says this quality is its own reward

explanation.surface: A woman named Patience is reputed to settle her own debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'virtue is its own reward' supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is one of the traditional moral qualities, an example of moral goodness.

clue.text: This offers food-value for some workers

definitions.text: This offers food-value for some workers

blocks.note: surface: the nutritional value of food

blocks.clueFragment: This offers food-value for some workers
blocks.note: setter's reading: a ticket worth a set sum towards a midday meal, given by employers

explanation.surface: Something that provides nourishing food to certain employees.
explanation.walkthrough: Luncheon vouchers were paper tickets British employers gave staff to spend on lunch at cafes.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticket is literally worth a monetary value redeemable for food, issued by some employers.

clue.text: A horse to watch

blocks.note: first meaning: a horse bred for riding to hounds
second meaning: a pocket watch with a hinged metal lid over its face

explanation.surface: A tipster's horse worth keeping an eye on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To watch' reads as a racing tip; watch is in fact a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a type of riding horse and a pocket timepiece with protective cover share this name.

clue.text: One Mediterranean port or another

blocks.note: first meaning: the capital of Libya
second meaning: a port city of the same name in northern Lebanon

explanation.surface: Someone can't decide which Mediterranean harbour to sail into.
explanation.definitionFit: Two separate coastal cities, in Libya and in Lebanon, carry this name.

clue.text: Regrettable squabble in a London park

definitions.note: names a place within the park

blocks.note: a rotten business is a regrettable one
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: An unfortunate quarrel breaks out in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is the horse-riding track along the south side of Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous bridle path runs through Hyde Park, so it is found inside a London park.

clue.text: Saw Jack - a splendid fellow!

blocks.note: first meaning: a ripsaw, which cuts along the grain
second meaning: the Victorian murderer's nickname
third meaning: old slang for an excellent person

explanation.surface: Someone spotted their friend Jack and greets him warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: 'Saw' is not a verb but a tool, and Jack points to the Whitechapel killer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cutting saw, the notorious London killer, and in dated slang a first-rate chap.

clue.text: Bookmaker for whom love isn't unusual?

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so those letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the two words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A betting agent who is no stranger to romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a racecourse betting man; read literally, it is someone who makes books. The words isn't and unusual both serve the wordplay, while the surface reads them as a denial.
explanation.definitionFit: An author of fiction literally produces books, so the crossword joke treats a writer as a maker of books.

clue.text: Film in which Clementine's father played a part

definitions.text: in which Clementine's father played a part

blocks.note: first meaning: Chaplin's 1925 silent comedy

blocks.clueFragment: in which Clementine's father played a part
blocks.note: second meaning: the 1849 California stampede, in which the song's miner, a forty-niner, took part

explanation.surface: A movie in which an actress's father had a role.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine', her father is 'a miner, forty-niner', one of those who rushed to California in 1849.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaplin's classic is titled after the frantic search for gold in Alaska, and the 1849 California prospecting boom was one.

clue.text: What artist's models do after this rest

definitions.text: What artist's models do after this

blocks.clueFragment: What artist's models do after this
blocks.note: first meaning: pose again, which sitters do after a break
second meaning: a state of calm or sleep

explanation.surface: Life models take up their positions again after a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points at the answer itself: after the rest, the models re-pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a noun for relaxation or a state of calm and stillness.

clue.text: Start to plead for admission

blocks.note: to beg is to plead
asking to be let in, so IN follows

explanation.surface: The opening move is to ask to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: Begging to come in, read as two words, makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, the two words both mean commence or set something going.

clue.text: Do ornithologists ring these varieties?

blocks.note: surface: birdwatchers put identification rings on birds' legs
setter's reading: ring as a bell does, so these are birds named for a bell-like call

explanation.surface: A question about which kinds of bird scientists fit with leg rings.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellbirds are several species, in New Zealand, Australia and South America, whose calls sound like a chime.
explanation.definitionFit: Several unrelated species share the name because their calls sound like chiming, so they are varieties of bird.

clue.text: Announcer using public address system

blocks.note: surface: loudspeakers wired up to make announcements
setter's reading: a man who shouts news through the streets, the old way of addressing the public

explanation.surface: Someone making announcements over the loudspeakers.
explanation.walkthrough: A town crier rang a handbell and called out proclamations in the market square.
explanation.definitionFit: This official's job was to make public announcements by shouting them out in the streets.

clue.text: Engineer with bias is lying

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
cum is Latin for with, as in a kitchen-cum-diner
a bent is a leaning or inclination

explanation.surface: A prejudiced engineer is telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' sounds like telling fibs but means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent describes someone reclining or lying down flat, the posture sense of lying.

clue.text: Sterne's corporal booked to the islands by boat

blocks.note: Corporal Trim is Uncle Toby's servant in Sterne's novel Tristram Shandy
the Aran Islands lie off Galway in western Ireland

explanation.surface: A literary corporal has a ticket to travel to the islands by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' nods to Trim being a character in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing vessel with a main hull and two outriggers, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Silvan setting for TV studios

blocks.note: first meaning: a stand of linden trees
second meaning: the BBC's studios in Shepherd's Bush, west London

explanation.surface: A woodland scene used as a backdrop for television.
explanation.walkthrough: Lime Grove Studios were a major BBC television centre from 1950 to 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation of linden trees is a woodland scene, and the BBC broadcast from studios of that name.

clue.text: For painter sea-mist is a problem

indicators.note: a problem is something in a mess, so those letters are muddled

blocks.note: the letters of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A painter of seascapes is hampered by fog rolling in.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French artist who led the Fauvist movement in painting.

clue.text: This driver for Rosinante?

blocks.note: surface: a kind of driver, as if naming a tool, a golfer or a coachman
setter's reading: Don Quixote's horse was a broken-down nag, and old slang has a word for such a horse that also completes the tool name

explanation.surface: Someone asks who rode Don Quixote's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosinante is Don Quixote's bony old horse; a worn-out horse was once called a screw.
explanation.definitionFit: In old horse-dealing slang the word means a decrepit, unsound nag like Quixote's mount.

clue.text: He tempts us to record about one hundred

indicators.note: about means going around, so the record wraps around what follows

blocks.note: to enter details is to record them
Roman numeral for one
Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A seducer persuades us to log about a hundred of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticer is a person who lures or tempts others into doing something.

clue.text: Harry's in South Dakota, it's said

indicators.note: in places one name inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: the US state's postal abbreviation
Harry Tate was a British music-hall comedian, so Harry's surname

explanation.surface: Someone reports that Harry is now in South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Tate was a famous British music-hall comic of the early 1900s.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated is a past participle meaning declared or put into words, just like said.

clue.text: Seat for Bismarck in the Museum

blocks.note: first meaning: the part of the body one sits on
second meaning: where the German battleship Bismarck ended up after it was sunk in 1941, the seabed

explanation.surface: A chair set aside for the German chancellor in a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: Bismarck reads as the statesman but is the sunk battleship; the museum phrase seems to be only surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the buttocks one sits upon and the floor of the ocean.

clue.text: Last month one new team has made the final

indicators.note: something new has been made over, so the word after it is rearranged

blocks.note: ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters
Roman numeral for one
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly formed side reached the cup final only last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' looks like a cup final, a noun; here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate is an adjective meaning last in a series, coming at the very end.

clue.text: Scientific work on the subject of a gun-catch gets award

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
the sear is the catch in a gun's lock that holds the hammer until the trigger is pulled
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A scientific paper about a gun's mechanism wins a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is the systematic investigation scientists carry out in laboratories to discover new facts.

clue.text: Position of fencing I erect is wrong

indicators.note: being wrong means not in the right order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A fencer admits their upright stance is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Position of fencing' could suggest putting up a garden fence; it is a stance in swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tierce is the third of the eight standard parrying positions in the sport of swordplay.

clue.text: Country journalist going in all directions

indicators.note: going in means entering, so the editor sits inside the string that follows

blocks.note: the four compass points: south, west, east, north
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A rural reporter rushing off every which way at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective for the journalist, as in a country vet; it is the definition, a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is the Scandinavian nation between Norway and Finland.

clue.text: In this bird the colour's sharp

blocks.note: red is a colour, and the 's adds S
a tart taste is a sharp, sour one

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher remarks that this bird's plumage is vivid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' in the name is Old English for tail: the bird has a rust-red tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with an orange-red tail that it constantly flicks.
